challenge.better_approach: Blanket-lowercase argv in the dispatcher. Rejected: argv carries free text and folding it would alter his verbatim. Per-site .lower() with no primitive. Rejected: the same settled answer written twenty times and nothing to grep for when the next seam appears.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That folding never collides two distinct system words (measured: every table and bin/ directory is lowercase-unique). That no keyword slot is also a free-text slot (learning_block disambiguates by SIGNALS membership). That no device bin/ has two entries differing only by case (none).

Lab consult (recompiled 2026-09-07): no charter states a case rule for keywords. argparse is case-sensitive by design, so its flags are folded before parse.
challenge.real_collision: ruling.py:138 and test_ruling.py:286-311 (lowercase 'ruled' must not confirm) vs this cast. Both matchers read only his text, and he ruled the case rule away with the marker in every case. Exclusive and terminal, settled by the ruling; the tooth flips and cites it.

value.what: Every system word in cairn (a status word, a command word, a marker, any keyword) matches case-insensitively at every seam where the text can come from Akien, with the `cairn` command itself the one lowercase exception.

value: A keyword that only matches in one case is a rule the operator has to remember, and a rule remembered is discipline doing physics' job (Law 4). The 2026-08-13 uppercase marker was itself a remembered rule ('I will start saying RULED after every goddamned one'), and it is the one that bit.
